page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. This virtual machine includes no local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying entirely on remote network-attached block storage for persistent filesystem operations.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate distinct multi-threaded scaling alongside moderate single-thread execution rates. Multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, rank in the top 25 percent of tested cloud hardware, reflecting effective utilization of the 96 virtual execution threads. In contrast, single-core metrics from stress-ng and Geekbench place in the middle 50 percent, aligned with the 2.8 GHz clock profile. Cryptographic capabilities are prominent, with PassMark CPU encryption tests scoring in the top 10 percent due to hardware AES and VAES vector extensions. Memory throughput remains robust across large block reads and writes, achieving 323.4 GB/sec and 131.45 GB/sec respectively, alongside strong in-memory key-value performance registering 87.92 million Redis SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is centered on high-density concurrent processing rather than isolated per-thread compute tasks. Because local scratch storage is omitted, total system architecture requires accounting for attached remote volumes for I/O operations. Workloads that do not utilize parallel threading will yield lower efficiency per resource allocated due to mid-tier single-core speeds. The hardware profile is optimal for distributed enterprise applications, relational database engines, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD compilation clusters, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D96s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory. Lacking local storage and discrete GPUs, the instance utilizes remote storage attachments for system and application data. Benchmark testing reveals strong multi-threaded performance, placing in the top 25 percent for parallel workloads like software compilation, multi-core stress operations, and large-block memory bandwidth. Cryptographic throughput reaches the top 10 percent via hardware VAES and SHA extensions, while single-threaded tasks align with average cloud medians. The server maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory architecture suited for multi-threaded enterprise services, Redis cache deployments, parallel compilation pipelines, and database servers.
